slides.title: Welcome to HTML Basics
slides.content:
# Welcome to HTML Basics 🌐

HyperText Markup Language (**HTML**) is the foundational building block of the World Wide Web. It defines the structure and meaning of web content.

## What you'll master in this module:
- 🏷️ **Tags & Elements** - Opening tags, closing tags, self-closing elements, and void tags
- ⚙️ **Attributes** - Modifying and providing essential metadata for elements
- 🏗️ **Document Structure** - Standard HTML5 boilerplate, doctype, and rendering modes
- 📝 **Core Text Formatting** - Headings, paragraphs, semantic emphasis, and text helpers
- 📋 **HTML Entities & Comments** - Handling reserved characters and writing maintainable code

> 💡 **Fun Fact:** HTML was originally created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1991 to help researchers share academic papers across networks!

slides.title: HTML Attributes Explained
slides.content: # HTML Attributes ⚙️ Attributes provide additional information, configuration, or behavior for an HTML element. ## Syntax Rules: - Attributes are **always** placed inside the **opening tag**. - Written as `name="value"` pairs. - Values should always be wrapped in quotes (double quotes are industry standard). ```html_not Visit Example ``` ### Breakdown: - `href`: Defines the hyperlink destination. - `target`: Specifies where to open the linked document (`_blank` opens a new tab). - `rel`: Sets security attributes (`noopener` prevents tab hijacking).

slides.title: Boolean Attributes
slides.content:
# Boolean Attributes 🔘

Boolean attributes represent true/false states. If the attribute is present on an element, its value is considered **true**; if absent, it is **false**.

```html_not
<!-- Checked and disabled inputs -->
<input type="checkbox" checked>
<button disabled>Cannot Click Me</button>
<video autoplay loop muted></video>
```

## Explicit vs Implicit Syntax
All of these evaluate to true in modern browsers:
- `<input required>` *(Preferred standard)*
- `<input required="required">`
- `<input required="">`

> ⚠️ **Gotcha:** Writing `<button disabled="false">` STILL disables the button because the attribute name `disabled` is present! To make it false, omit the attribute entirely.

slides.title: The DOCTYPE & Quirks Mode
slides.content:
# The DOCTYPE Declaration 📜

The `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration tells web browsers which specification of HTML is being used.

```html_not
<!DOCTYPE html>
```

## Why is DOCTYPE Critical?
- **Standards Mode:** When `<!DOCTYPE html>` is present at the very top (line 1), browsers render following modern W3C standards.
- **Quirks Mode:** If the DOCTYPE is omitted or corrupted, the browser drops into "Quirks Mode" to emulate 1990s Netscape/IE bugs, breaking CSS box model layouts and font sizes!

> 💡 **Notice:** `<!DOCTYPE html>` is not an HTML tag; it is an instruction to the web browser engine.

slides.title: The Head & Metadata
slides.content:
# The <head> and Metadata 🧠

The `<head>` element holds meta-information about the webpage that browsers and search engines read.

```html_not
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="description" content="Free comprehensive HTML tutorial">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
  <link rel="icon" href="favicon.ico">
  <title>Mastering HTML Basics</title>
</head>
```

## Key Head Tags:
- `<meta charset="UTF-8">`: Specifies character encoding to support all international characters and emojis.
- `<meta name="viewport" ...>`: Essential for responsive web design on mobile devices.
- `<title>`: Shown in the browser tab and search engine search results (SERP).

slides.title: Semantic Text Formatting
slides.content:
# Semantic Text Formatting ✍️

HTML provides tags that convey semantic importance rather than just visual styling.

| Semantic Tag | Visual Style | Semantic Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `<strong>` | **Bold** | High importance or seriousness |
| `<em>` | *Italic* | Stress emphasis (spoken inflection) |
| `<mark>` | Highlighted | Marked or highlighted for relevance |
| `<del>` | ~~Strikethrough~~ | Deleted or retracted text |
| `<ins>` | Underlined | Newly inserted text |
| `<sub>` | H₂O (subscript)| Subscript baseline offset |
| `<sup>` | E=mc² (superscript)| Superscript exponent offset |

> 🎯 **Accessibility Tip:** Screen readers announce `<strong>` and `<em>` with vocal inflection, whereas `<b>` and `<i>` are purely stylistic tags without semantic meaning.

slides.title: HTML Entities & Special Characters
slides.content:
# HTML Entities & Characters 🔣 Because characters like `<` and `>` are reserved for HTML syntax, you must use **HTML entities** to display them as regular text. ## Common HTML Entities: | Character | Entity Name | Entity Number | Meaning | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `<` | `<` | `<` | Less than | | `>` | `>` | `>` | Greater than | | `&` | `&` | `&` | Ampersand | | `"` | `"` | `"` | Double quote | | `'` | `'` | `'` | Single quote / apostrophe | | ` ` | ` ` | ` ` | Non-breaking space | | `©` | `©` | `©` | Copyright symbol | ```html_not

To write an opening tag, type <div> & close with </div>.

Copyright © 2026 CodeCerebrum. All rights reserved.

```

slides.title: HTML Comments & Documentation
slides.content:
# HTML Comments 💬 Comments allow developers to document code, explain complex layouts, or temporarily disable elements without deleting them. ```html_not
Sign In
``` ## Rules for Comments: - Browser rendering engines completely ignore everything between ``. - Comments are **visible** in the client-side page source (never put API keys or passwords inside comments!).
